reference: GNU coreutils pathchk invoked by the reference Bash from /usr/bin:/bin; its default filesystem limits and POSIX -p checks are independent of the candidate. POSIX portable filename characters and the 14-byte component and 255-byte pathname minima provide the documented -p boundaries.
coverage: Default mode accepts relative paths and checks the fixture filesystem's component and whole-path limits.
-p accepts portable characters, honors --, and enforces the POSIX component and whole-path length limits.
A regular file used as a leading path component is rejected as not a directory.
Missing operands produce an error status.
Bash type metadata reports pathchk as a builtin.
Search-denied directory, symlink directory prefix, empty pathname, and repeated-call option state.
Empty pathnames are rejected in default and portability modes.
exclusions: Filesystem-specific 255/4096 default limits are Linux fixture assumptions, checked against the reference before candidate classification. Exact diagnostic wording is not compared.

cases.purpose: Check that ordinary relative names, repeated separators, dot components, --, and a 255-byte component are accepted in default mode.
On the fixture filesystem, verify that a 256-byte component exceeds NAME_MAX.
Verify acceptance of a 4095-byte relative pathname, immediately below the fixture filesystem's 4096-byte PATH_MAX; all components remain below NAME_MAX.
cases.script: printf -v component '%*s' 240 ''; component=${component// /x}; printf -v final '%*s' 239 ''; final=${final// /x}; path=$component; for ((i=1; i<16; i++)); do path=$path/$component; done; path=$path/$final; pathchk "$path"

cases.purpose: Verify that extending a 4095-byte relative pathname by one byte reaches the fixture filesystem's 4096-byte PATH_MAX and is rejected; all components remain within NAME_MAX.
cases.script: printf -v component '%*s' 240 ''; component=${component// /x}; printf -v final '%*s' 239 ''; final=${final// /x}; path=$component; for ((i=1; i<16; i++)); do path=$path/$component; done; path=$path/$final; path=${path}x; pathchk "$path"

cases.purpose: Check portable ASCII characters, option termination for a path beginning with a dash, and acceptance of a 14-byte component.
Check that a 15-byte portable component exceeds the POSIX portable component limit.
Check that a space, which is outside the POSIX portable filename character set, is rejected by -p.
Check acceptance of a 255-byte portable relative pathname, the POSIX portable pathname limit.
cases.script: path=x; for ((i=1; i<128; i++)); do path=$path/x; done; pathchk -p "$path"

cases.purpose: Check that extending a 255-byte portable relative pathname by one byte exceeds the POSIX portable pathname limit.
cases.script: path=x; for ((i=1; i<128; i++)); do path=$path/x; done; path=${path}x; pathchk -p "$path"

cases.purpose: Create a small regular file with shell redirection and verify that pathchk rejects it when it is an existing leading component of a longer pathname.
Check the GNU CLI's missing-operand failure and reveal status differences in the Bash builtin usage path.
Check Bash type metadata for the statically available pathchk builtin without invoking its pathname operation.
Repeated builtin calls keep the -p flag local to each invocation.
cases.script: pathchk -p 'portable'; pathchk 'name with spaces'; if pathchk -p 'name with spaces'; then exit 1; fi; pathchk 'name with spaces'

cases.purpose: Reject an existing directory without search permission; capture the failure and restore fixture permissions before tree inspection.
cases.script: mkdir locked; chmod 600 locked; if pathchk locked/child; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi; chmod 700 locked; exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Follow an ordinary relative symlink to a searchable directory while validating its child pathname.
cases.script: mkdir real; ln -s real alias; pathchk alias/child

cases.purpose: Reject an empty pathname in default mode with GNU status 1 and a diagnostic.
Reject an empty pathname under -p with GNU status 1 and a diagnostic.
